title: Upstream sources allowlist
description: The declared, hash-pinned set of third-party binaries bin/upstream-fetch.mjs may fetch. Anything not declared here is refused; adding one is a tracked edit reviewed as a commit, which is the only human-in-the-loop step.

supersededSources.description: Sources deliberately NOT to be re-adopted. An archived repo still serves release assets, so a successful download is not evidence that a source is current.

sha256.description: Required. A declaration with no hash is refused rather than fetched — 'no hash' must not be the easy path.

publisherChecksums.description: Whether the RELEASE itself publishes checksums. false means our sha256 is a first-observation pin, not a confirmation against the publisher — a materially weaker claim that must not be flattened into 'verified'.

kind.description: binary (default, may be omitted): the asset is used as-is. rulepack: the asset is a rule-pack archive; after its sha256 is verified, bin/upstream-fetch.mjs extracts it and hash-adjacent-records which rules it contains (see ruleFormat) — the same hash-pinned-source discipline applied to a third-party ruleset instead of a binary, so a 'ruleset-dependent' coverage entry in cwe-map.json can eventually cite exact rule ids.

ruleFormat.description: Required when kind is 'rulepack' — enforced at RUNTIME in bin/upstream-fetch.mjs's extractRulepack() (an unrecognised or absent ruleFormat throws before extraction runs), not in this schema. monitor/registry.mjs's schema checker is a deliberately small draft-07 subset (SCHEMA_KEYWORDS) that does not implement allOf/if/then, and an unimplemented keyword is a hard ERROR there ('quietly ignoring the unevaluable is how a schema goes decorative') rather than something to add speculatively to a load-bearing, shared validator for one new field.
